items.title: Persist red-target-bindings.json through StoryStore with exactly one binding per acceptance target
items.context: packages/main/src/core/store.ts gains read/write for .lattice/story/actives/<id>/red-target-bindings.json (schema proofstory.red_target_bindings.v1); the store enforces the §1.1.3 uniqueness invariant of exactly one binding per acceptanceTargetRef (a second write for the same ref is a duplicate-target rejection, not an overwrite). Types in core/types.ts:69 area declare the binding entry and the v1 file shape.

happy.desc: Write a valid binding {acceptanceTargetRef:"AB-001/hash-aaa", adapterId:"node-test-runner", testCaseRef:"test/red/a.test.ts"} -> persists one entry in red-target-bindings.json with schema proofstory.red_target_bindings.v1, three identity fields plus createdAt; WHY: proves store layer round-trips a single binding
Write a SECOND binding for a DIFFERENT acceptanceTargetRef -> appends (bindings array length = 2), both entries intact; WHY: proves append semantics, not replace-all

edge.desc: Read from a story with no existing red-target-bindings.json -> returns empty bindings array or null, no crash; WHY: covers cold-start / new-story path
Write a binding where acceptanceTargetRef contains slash, hash, and unicode (e.g. AB-999/req#special) -> persists with exact field values round-tripped; WHY: boundary on ref format

adversarial.desc: Write a SECOND binding for the SAME acceptanceTargetRef that already has a stored binding -> rejected as duplicate-target (NOT overwrite); original binding remains unchanged; WHY: enforces section 1.1.3 exactly-one-per-target uniqueness invariant
Two rapid sequential writes for two different targets -> both persist without corruption or partial write; WHY: serialization safety under fast successive calls

items.title: Compute targetBindingDigest over the createdAt-stripped three-field subobject only
items.context: The recorded targetBindingDigest is CANON (W2a canon.ts) over exactly the three binding-identity fields with createdAt STRIPPED; a stored entry carries createdAt, so CANON over the STORED entry must NOT equal the digest while CANON over the stripped three-field subobject MUST. This createdAt-strip direction is the behavioral RED trap a naive implementation gets wrong.

items.title: Export expectedRedTargets as one shared resolver and gate binding writes on target membership
items.context: The currently module-private expectedRedTargets (packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:887) is extracted as a shared exported resolver WITHOUT changing its computed set (proven by a same-set assertion). red_evidence_binding_set rejects at write time (§3.3) any acceptanceTargetRef not in expectedRedTargets.

items.title: Resolve the authorizing binding from a committed tree ref and never from the live story directory
items.context: A committed-tree reader resolves a binding from <ref>:.lattice/story/actives/<id>/red-target-bindings.json via git show, NOT from the live (possibly edited) story directory; a test where the committed tree and the live directory hold different bindings proves the reader returns the committed one (§1.1.3 committed-tree lookup).

items.title: Register red-target-bindings.json in the lifecycle artifact set and the ProofStory artifact path list
items.context: Add the filename to LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES (core/lifecycle-registry.ts:599) so the scope classifier (rejects unknown top-level story artifacts at :849) accepts it as lifecycle metadata, and to the ProofStory artifact path list. This closes RED signal A (a story touching the file can now reach DONE).

items.title: Register red_evidence_binding_set at every wiring point including the closed mutation-command union
items.context: Register the command in registry.ts (MAIN_TOOLS), cli/command-catalog.ts, core/command-policy.ts, core/config.ts, core/process-fact-levels.ts, core/process-fact-registry.ts, AND the two points the spec never names: the CLOSED AgentDispatchMutationCommand union at core/types.ts:69 and the per-role permittedMutations arrays (core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:435). The existing lifecycle-registry-contract.ts + command-ownership-contract.ts (RED signal B) enumerate these bidirectionally and pass only when all are present.

items.title: Gate the command through the owner lease and resolved agent mutation authority
items.context: red_evidence_binding_set flows through the single CLI choke point (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1372) as a storyScopedMutating ownership class gated by enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate, and by resolveAgentMutationAuthority (core/agent-dispatch-registry.ts:504) via entryPermitsMutation (:435). The command is rejected while a FOREIGN session holds an active owner lease (§4.1).

items.title: Update the four hard-coded ProofStory command enumerations and the frozen catalog order assertion
items.context: Update the FOUR hard-coded ProofStory command enumerations in scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs (the process-fact-levels map near :160 plus the three MAIN_TOOLS command-name enumeration arrays near :1013, :1229, :1265) and the frozen trailing-order assertion at packages/main/src/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.ts:102-109 so the new command's catalog position is asserted; verify-process-fact-contract.mjs passes only when all four enumerations include the command.

items.title: Register red-evidence-target-binding-smoke in lattice.config.json validate.commands and prove no gate verdict changes
items.context: Create packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-target-binding-smoke.ts covering the store uniqueness, the createdAt-strip digest both directions, the expectedRedTargets same-set + membership gate, the committed-tree reader, the owner-lease/foreign-lease rejection, and the full registration surface; register it in lattice.config.json validate.commands. Prove NO existing gate verdict changes: redEvidenceSatisfied / missingRedEvidence and all existing gates are untouched (this story adds a store + command, rewires no gate).
